confirmed_findings.claim: Run and RunSync are near-total byte-for-byte code duplication, differing only in the timeout constant and error-message prefix, so any future fix to the run mechanics must be applied twice.
confirmed_findings.fix: Factor a shared unexported run(ctx context.Context, timeout time.Duration, label, dir, name string, args ...string) (string, error) and make Run/RunSync thin callers passing their own timeout/label.

confirmed_findings.claim: The persisted audience value was renamed from "non-developer" to "casual", contradicting the approved plan's explicit D5 decision that only the two existing values are ever written, with no plan Decisions amendment or Changelog row (RULE-PLAN-049).
confirmed_findings.fix: Flag for explicit confirmation: if the rename was deliberate, update D5/D6 and add the Changelog row; if not, keep "non-developer" as the constant value with "Casual" only as the UI label.

confirmed_findings.claim: The build-install target's help comment is a copy-paste of build's, so make help shows a bogus/duplicate build row instead of documenting build-install.

Add/Remove's read-modify-write against a fresh readRegistrySnapshot narrows but does not fully close the multi-process race: two processes racing within the same read-to-write window can still silently drop one write since there is no OS-level file lock.
confirmed_findings.fix: Add a one-line comment acknowledging the residual window, or an flock-style guard if concurrent configservers become a real scenario again.

confirmed_findings.claim: The "was a context file read via Bash" detector only recognizes the literal two-word form `cat <path>` and bails out on any shell metacharacter, so any other reader (less, python3 -c, \cat, a heredoc) evades detection entirely.
squash_contained()'s comment says "no side effects", but git merge-tree --write-tree does write a garbage-collectible tree object into the ODB, so the comment is slightly over-stated.
The guard `[[ "$exit_status" -eq 0 ]] && exit_status=$orchestrate_status` is a tautology since the enclosing if at line 94 already requires exit_status -eq 0 and nothing mutates it before this line.
